title: Construction of pilot Elena-AM microreactor 'under way'
html:
The inclusion of the information was reported by the Atominfo website, which said the document was published on 26 November.

According to the strategy, "construction is under way in the Republic of Sakha (Yakutia) on the first low-power land-based nuclear power plant, 'Elena-AM', with an electric capacity of up to 400 kW and a heating capacity of up to 14 MW".

No further details are given. In June 2021, World Nuclear News reported that Russia's state nuclear corporation Rosatom aimed to launch pilot units called Shelf-M (up to 10 MWe) and Elena-AM (400 kWe and 5 Gcal/h) in remote regions of the country.

In 2023, a Rosatom newsletter carried a feature called 'The Return of Elena' which said Elena-AM was a pilot plant under development for Rosatom at the Kurchatov Institute. It said the original Elena concept was developed in 1989/1990 for a pilot cogeneration plant to supply heat and power to a research station operated by the Pacific Oceanological Institute near Elena Bay on Popov Island. It was to be able to generate 880 kW of electricity and 3 MW of heat. "However, the project was never put into practice due to a lack of finance and poor economic conditions in the country," the article says.

The revived idea - AM stands for automated and upgraded - is for a unit "to serve as a source of heat in remote and hard-to-access regions that have no heat networks and are too distant and costly to supply with conventional fossil fuels".

With natural circulation of coolant in its two circuits, Elena-AM has a planned service life of 40 years. The newsletter reported that the 120-centimetre high reactor core would consist of 241 assemblies with fuel enriched to no more than 19.5%. It would be able to operate in a load-following mode, ranging from 20% to 100% of its nominal capacity.

The newsletter article adds: "The plant will operate 350 days a year and then be shut down for two weeks for diagnostics and maintenance. Maintenance and repairs are planned to be done annually by a dedicated mobile team during the two-week break."

Russia has also developed the Shelf-M microreactor, an integral nuclear power plant with a pressurised water reactor capable of generating 10 MWe/35 MWt. A pilot plant is proposed, to supply power for the Sovinoye gold deposit in Chukotka in Russia's far east. It would need refuelling every eight years and have a 60-year design life. Earlier this year Rosatom said a construction schedule had been developed, engineering surveys for the site had begun, and the project's investment justification was nearing completion.
summary: The Strategy for the Development of the Arctic Zone of the Russian Federation and Ensuring National Security in the Arctic says that construction is under way on a pilot Elena-AM microreactor.  ;
